comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
You can reproduce this issue by downloading the latest GitHub release (electron-v33.1.0-linux-x64 at the time of testing). To see the issue, run the binary as `./electron --ozone-platform-hint=auto` on a Wayland session. 
The problem will become apparent as you observe the inability to resize the client window.

The last known working version that allowed window resizing was v31, although it had the CSD border issue described in #42894  It seems likely that a change introduced between v31 and the current release may be causing this behavior.

Please let me know if any additional details or specific configurations are needed.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Hi @participant17 @participant19 

Apologies for the ping, and I hope I’m reaching out to the right people. From what I understand, you both might have the knowledge and expertise to help progress this issue (apologies if not).

I’ve bisected with electron fiddle and noticed that the resize issue seems to have originated between 32.0.0-alpha.5 (working resize) and 32.0.0-alpha.6 (broken resize). Interestingly, while alpha.6 appears to have resolved #42894, it also introduced the resizing issue we see in this issue, and I’m unsure of the direct relation or the specific commit involved. Replication can easily be done by running electron binary on a Wayland Session (in my case GNOME Wayland) with ./electron --ozone-platform-hint=auto

I tried my best to narrow this down further to specific commits but ran into challenges compiling from source. This has become a pretty big blocker for Wayland adoption, as many downstream projects are intentionally staying on a deprecated version of Electron and can’t move forward.

Any chance we could take another look at the priority of this issue when you have a moment? Thanks so much for your time ❤

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
Agree on that one. `electron31` is the last release that can be resized normally. With `electron32` it started. 

Perhaps we should look at what changes were made when we jumped from version 31 to version 32 and revert this step by step. 


Also keep in mind that there are some new flags for Wayland in Chromium that need to be activated separately:

- `Wayland per-window scaling`
- `Wayland text-input-v3`
- `Wayland UI scaling`
- `Wayland linux-drm-syncobj explicit sync`

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Alright, first of all—wow! Compiling Electron from source is definitely not for the faint of heart (or the impatient). It’s taken me the better part of two days to bisect as best I could, but I’m hopeful it’s been worth the effort! 😛 That said, I believe I’ve identified the issue commits. I’ve documented the earliest Electron release versions where we first observed these regressions, and further down, I’ve pinpointed the exact commit where the issues initially appeared. For reference, I’ve also linked the backports—just a heads-up, both issues seem to have originated from Chromium bumps.

To clarify further, the problem extends beyond the resize regression discussed in this issue. It’s likely that both this and the [incorrect CSD/inset](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/42894#issuecomment-2351622791) issue share a common root cause. Which also seemingly only occurs on ozone/wayland with compositors that dont support SSD (ie. reference implementation Weston and also GNOME Wayland)

Earliest we seen this in Releases:
- CSD Inset Regression first seen on [31.0.0-beta.1](https://github.com/electron/electron/compare/v31.0.0-alpha.5...v31.0.0-beta.1)
- Resize Regression first seen on [32.0.0-alpha.6](https://github.com/electron/electron/compare/v32.0.0-alpha.5...v32.0.0-alpha.6)


## Further drill down to the affected earliest commits:

### First Affected Commit (CSD Border Issue)

The CSD/inset issue started with the following commit:

`chore: bump chromium to 126.0.6445.0 (31-x-y)` (#42119)

The above included:

- **Upstream Chromium Change**: [5367794: wayland: Support window state and insets in configure-sync model](https://<redacted-host>/c/chromium/src/+/5367794)
- **Electron Implementation**: [Address Linux NonClientFrameView Changes](https://github.com/electron/electron/commit/dff980c9c20da444fb853b6983eb75d48714b486)


Later, the Chromium developers reverted the upstream change, then re-landed it with code changes:

- **Revert Commit**: [5404542](https://<redacted-host>/c/chromium/src/+/5404542) (might also be worth noting they reverted changes due to ci [failures](https://<redacted-host>/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/Linux%20Tests%20(Wayland)/54825/overview) for the linux wayland tests using weston)
- **Re-land Commit**: [5416939](https://<redacted-host>/c/chromium/src/+/5416939/1..36)

You can compare the original patchset (1) with the re-landed patchset (36) on the re-land commit link to review the code changes.


### Second Affected Commit (This Issue)
**On the Electron end:**

The re-landed Chromium changes were pulled in and this is when the resize issue (this issue) first started to occur:

`chore: bump chromium to 128.0.6558.0 (32-x-y)` (#42746)

Testing these upstream Chromium changes with Chromium itself, I was not able to reproduce the issue, which leads me to believe it may likely be the Electron implementation commit [Address Linux NonClientFrameView Changes](https://github.com/electron/electron/commit/dff980c9c20da444fb853b6983eb75d48714b486).

The Electron changes may need to be reviewed again since upstream Chromium have re-landed theirs with new code changes. We may need to potentially look at the original Electron side implementation again as well and see why we ran into the CSD regression, but I suspect it may be the same root cause.

I don’t have deep knowledge of the codebase since my focus is primarily in QA, but I hope someone more familiar with the Electron codebase can make use of this information.

Not sure who to ping on this (just going on who was involved in the commits/reviews) since I know some of the team are on a quiet period, but hoping any of the talented engineers who have availability can at least offer some guidance/further comments here at all?
cc @participant17 @participant20 @participant21 @participant22 @participant19

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
First, thanks for your work, mate. 

In addition to your assumption:

https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/42894 can also be triggered with a Chromium-based browser and the [Rounded Window Corners Reborn Extension](https://github.com/flexagoon/rounded-window-corners)

If the window is minimized with the extension activated, exactly the same behavior occurs. 
I noticed this about 3–4 days ago with a stable version of Brave. At that time, `Wayland linux-drm-syncobj explicit sync` was not implemented in the stable branch. 

Since I am currently not working with Gnome, I can't check if the same behavior can still be triggered if `Wayland linux-drm-syncobj explicit sync` is activated. 

However, the behavior there is even more exciting because the entire UI is scaled incorrectly then, which is probably due to the lack of fractional scaling. 

Hope this helps to narrow down the problem further.
